question: Can a Mamba2 state-space model be trained once as nested widths so deployment can choose compute dynamically without training a separate model at every size?

key_findings.claim: Slicing every hidden-dimension-dependent Mamba2 parameter creates nested submodels that can be optimized jointly in one universal checkpoint.
key_findings.evidence: The model defines four granularities, computes a loss for each explicit slice, and backpropagates their sum so smaller models share prefixes of the largest model's weights.

key_findings.claim: Explicit nested widths largely match independently trained Mamba2 baselines in the reported vision and language settings.
key_findings.evidence: Across 35M/135M ImageNet models and 130M-1.4B FineWeb language models, explicit granularities track scratch Mamba2 accuracy or perplexity while residing in one model.

key_findings.claim: Mix-and-match widths provide many unseen compute points, but the smallest interpolated configurations can degrade late in training.
key_findings.evidence: Layerwise mixtures between trained granularities produce a dense quality-cost curve; the language experiments note late-training degradation for smaller non-explicit mixtures, indicating interference is not fully solved.

method.core_idea: Embed several Mamba2 widths as prefix slices of one parameter tensor and jointly minimize their losses.
method.mechanism: Each training example runs the explicit granularities, shared parameters accumulate gradients from all widths, and inference selects a uniform or layerwise mixed granularity.
assumptions: Prefix slicing preserves a meaningful nested subspace in each Mamba2 block.
Four explicitly trained widths sufficiently support interpolation to unseen layerwise mixtures.
Extra multi-width training compute is acceptable when amortized over deployments.

techniques.role: Makes smaller SSMs exact parameter slices of the largest model.
Creates unseen intermediate compute budgets at inference.

evaluations.setting: ImageNet classification with 35M and 135M vision backbones
evaluations.metric: Top-1 accuracy versus parameters and throughput
evaluations.result: Nested explicit widths match or improve similarly sized scratch Mamba2 models; Mamba becomes faster than ViT at high resolutions in reported H100 tests.

evaluations.setting: FineWeb language modeling from 130M to 1.4B parameters
evaluations.result: Explicit widths follow independently trained Mamba2 scaling curves, while some small interpolated mixtures degrade late.
evaluations.baseline: Scratch Mamba2 models at corresponding sizes

evaluations.metric: Compute reduction at bounded accuracy loss
evaluations.result: The 135M model reduces compute by about 55% for less than 0.5 percentage-point accuracy loss.

limitations: Joint training requires multiple forward passes per sample even though backward memory resembles the largest model.
Experiments cover standard image and language tasks rather than real cloud-edge or speculative-decoding systems.
Late-training degradation of small interpolated mixtures shows that untrained configurations are not uniformly reliable.
failure_modes: Shared prefixes can receive conflicting gradients from large and small widths.
Arbitrary layerwise mixtures may fall outside the combinations supported by explicit training.
A universal checkpoint saves model-management cost but not storage relative to the full model.
reusable_insights: Elastic-model evaluations should distinguish explicitly optimized submodels from post-hoc interpolations.
Deployment value depends on quality-compute frontiers and switching policy, not only average accuracy.
Nested representations can be applied to structured sequence blocks by slicing all coupled dimensions consistently.
open_questions: Can sampling or distillation reduce the multi-width training overhead without harming small slices?
Which runtime policy should select widths under latency, energy, and uncertainty constraints?
Does nested Mamba remain stable at longer contexts and multi-billion-parameter scale?

competitive_landscape.title: MatFormer: Nested Transformer for Elastic Inference
competitive_landscape.difference: MatFormer nests transformer feed-forward dimensions; MatMamba adapts nesting to the coupled projections and state-space structure of Mamba2.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
competitive_landscape.difference: Mamba2 introduces the structured state-space block; MatMamba adds jointly trained elastic widths and inference-time mixtures.

competitive_landscape.title: Once-for-All: Train One Network and Specialize it for Efficient Deployment
competitive_landscape.difference: Once-for-All progressively trains and specializes CNN subnets; MatMamba uses prefix-nested SSM dimensions and direct joint losses for sequence and vision models.

competitive_landscape.title: Matryoshka Representation Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: MRL nests useful embedding prefixes, while MatMamba nests executable internal model widths across all layers.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: nested representations, once-for-all subnetworks, and MatFormer are established. The distinct contribution is a consistent nesting rule for Mamba2 blocks plus image/language evidence that explicit widths and many mixtures form usable elastic SSMs.
reviewer_notes: Full paper and appendices were checked, including training cost, throughput, explicit-width, interpolation, and retrieval results. Primary competitor records checked 2026-08-23.
